subject: MSA + Order Form: breach-specific cap and security addendum linkage
messages:
From: Kate Ryan <kate.ryan@acme.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: jane.doe@acme.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA redlines — breach liability carve-out (v3)

Evelyn,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our MSA redline (Acme-MSA-redlines-v3.docx) and a short note from our security team. The key open item from our side is the breach-specific liability sub-limit: we are proposing a $2M sub-limit for liabilities arising from data security incidents, with an explicit carve-out for willful misconduct.

We understand Redwood's standard cap is 3x fees / $10M (whichever is lower). For regulated data we need that specific sub-limit in the contract plus explicit mapping to obligations in the Security Addendum. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can:

- Accept a $2M sub-limit for security incidents tied to the Security Addendum; and
- Preserve general liability cap language for other breaches and non-security liabilities?

Also attaching a PDF summary from our InfoSec lead (Security-Addendum-proposed.pdf).

Next steps: please circulate to legal and ops; we need a final MSA by end of next week to sync with our procurement timelines.

Best,
Kate
Kate Ryan
Sr. Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme-MSA-redlines-v3.docx (docx, 78KB)
Attachment: Security-Addendum-proposed.pdf (pdf, 92KB)

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood MSA redlines — breach liability carve-out (v3)

Laura / Karthik — forwarding Acme's proposed redlines. They want a $2M sub-limit specifically for data security incidents and an explicit linkage to the Security Addendum. Procurement timeline is tight (they asked for final MSA by next Friday).

Quick context: Acme is a mid-market regulated customer; deal value ~$150k/mo. Sales (Karthik) flagged that accepting a standalone $2M sub-limit that sits under the general cap would be preferable to wholesale cap increases. Legal, please advise on negotiation posture we can take that balances risk and closability.

Questions for legal:
- Can we accept a security-specific sub-limit of $2M if we add clarifying language tying it to breach scenarios where Redwood is found to have breached its obligations under the Security Addendum?
- Would we preserve the general cap (3x fees / $10M) for all other liabilities? Any redline language you recommend to avoid overlap/ambiguity?
- Should we add a carve-out for third-party indemnities or regulatory fines? Acme is asking for clarity on what the sub-limit covers.

Karthik: any commercial flexibility on credits/discounts if we push back on the sub-limit?

Thanks — Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Principal, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA redlines — breach liability carve-out (v3)

Evelyn — thank you for the note and attachments. High-level legal take: we can likely accept a security-specific sub-limit, but only with careful drafting that ties the sub-limit to the Security Addendum obligations and excludes:

- Regulatory fines and penalties (we should reserve that as uncapped or carve in only to the extent permitted by law);
- Third-party claims covered by indemnity obligations (we should ensure IP and third-party indemnities are not swallowed by the sub-limit unless expressly stated);
- Willful misconduct should not be protected — we should maintain a standard exception.

Proposed approach (redline guidance):
1) Add a new clause: "For the avoidance of doubt, liabilities arising directly from Redwood's breach of its representations, warranties, or obligations under the Security Addendum ("Security Liabilities") shall be subject to a specific monetary sub-limit of $2,000,000. Security Liabilities do not include regulatory fines or third-party indemnifiable claims unless expressly stated herein."

2) Preserve the existing general liability cap (3x fees / $10M) for all other liabilities. Add cross-reference language so the sub-limit operates as a specialized cap for Security Liabilities only and does not reduce Acme's remedies under the Security Addendum for injunctive relief or equitable relief.

3) Include survivability: Security sub-limit applies to claims arising during the term and within 12 months after termination when the claim concerns an incident that occurred during the term.

I'll attach a short redline excerpt for Evelyn to share (I will upload separately). If Acme insists on including regulatory penalties under the sub-limit, we should push back hard — that's a material risk for Redwood.

Markus — flagging for additional exceptions (regulatory/insurance interplay).

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA redlines — breach liability carve-out (v3)

Team — thanks. Commercial note: Acme is on a fast procurement cadence; sales priority is to keep contract friction low. We are comfortable with the $2M security sub-limit if legal can ensure: (a) regulatory fines are excluded; and (b) the sub-limit only applies where Redwood materially failed to meet Security Addendum obligations. We can offer a one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to 1 month of service) as a compromise if they press hard on expanding the cap.

No change to list price otherwise. Evelyn, I can push that credit as a closing incentive.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kate Ryan <kate.ryan@acme.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: jane.doe@acme.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — breach liability carve-out (v3)

Evelyn — appreciate the quick turnaround and Laura's redline guidance. Acme is willing to accept the proposed formulation provided:

- The Security Addendum is explicitly cross-referenced and the Security Liabilities definition is linked to Redwood's failure to comply with the Security Addendum obligations;
- Regulatory fines arising solely from Acme's obligations or actions remain excluded from the sub-limit; and
- The survivability window is at least 12 months post-termination (we can accept 12 months).

We reviewed the suggested language and it looks workable. We'll incorporate Laura's excerpt into our next redline pass and aim to finalize the MSA by Friday. If Redwood can confirm the onboarding credit (one month) we can sign within the same week.

Thanks — Kate
